title: Magnetism
question: What is magnetism?

principle.name: Magnetism
principle.formulaNote: force on a moving charge = charge × velocity × field, at right angles to both. For a wire carrying current I across a field B: F = B × I × L. Fields are measured in tesla: Earth ≈ 25–65 µT, a fridge magnet ≈ 5 mT, an MRI scanner 1.5–3 T.
principle.idea: Magnets and electric currents fill the space around them with a magnetic field. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract, and a current in a field gets a sideways push, which is how motors, loudspeakers and MRI scanners work.
principle.discovered: c. 600 BCE lodestone (Thales, attributed); 1600 · William Gilbert, De Magnete; 1820 · Hans Christian Ørsted

examples.title: The MRI scanner's giant magnet
examples.text: A superconducting coil at −269 °C makes 1.5 or 3 T down the tunnel, about 30,000 to 60,000 times the Earth's field, with no power needed to keep it going.

examples.title: The magnetron's ring magnets
examples.text: Two ring magnets make about 0.17 T along the magnetron, curling its electrons past copper cavities so they ring at 2.45 GHz.

examples.title: A fan's induction motor
examples.text: Two coils fed a little out of step make a field that rotates, and the rotor is dragged round after it: no brushes, no magnets.

examples.title: A mixer's universal motor
examples.text: Field coils and a brushed commutator, the textbook DC motor on mains, spin the blades at up to about 22,000 rpm with no load.

examples.title: The inverter's transformer
examples.text: Two coils on one iron core turn the battery's 12 V into 230 V: the voltage changes by the ratio of the turns.

examples.title: Pickups and the amp's speaker
examples.text: A magnet under each string makes the steel string magnetic; its wiggle makes a signal in the coil, and at the other end a magnet and voice coil push the speaker cone.

examples.title: An electric car's motor
examples.text: Most electric cars drive their wheels with a permanent-magnet motor packed with neodymium magnets, giving full twist from standstill.

examples.title: The synth's loudspeaker
examples.text: Everything in a synth is voltage until the end, when a coil in a magnet's gap pushes a paper cone in and out: F = B I L at work.

examples.title: A compass on a trek
examples.text: A magnetised needle lines up with the Earth's field of 25–65 µT. Over India it points within a degree or two of true north.

examples.title: The scrapyard crane
examples.text: A 1.5 m electromagnet lifts a scrap car when switched on and drops it the instant the current is cut.

hook: Iron filings trace invisible curves, a wire with current in it swings a compass, and a coil with an iron core lifts a car. Map fields in tesla, spin a motor, curl electrons in a magnetron, flip the Earth's field and heat a nail past 770 °C.

explainer.title: Poles, fields and the tesla
explainer.text: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract. A magnet's field runs out of north and into south, and iron filings and compasses line up along it. Field is measured in tesla: the Earth is 25–65 µT, a fridge magnet about 5 mT, an MRI 1.5–3 T. The force between magnets falls off steeply with distance.

explainer.title: Current makes a magnet
explainer.text: Ørsted found in 1820 that a current's field circles the wire, B = μ₀ I ÷ 2πr. Coil the wire and the field inside is B = μ₀ n I; add an iron core and it grows hundreds of times, until the iron saturates. Cranes, bells, relays and door locks are switchable magnets.

explainer.title: A current in a field feels a push
explainer.text: F = B I L, at right angles to field and current (Fleming's left hand). A coil with a commutator becomes a DC motor whose back-EMF chokes the current as it speeds up. A loudspeaker shakes a coil in a 1 T gap to push air.

explainer.title: Magnets in machines
explainer.text: A superconducting MRI magnet at 1.5–3 T, a magnetron's 0.17 T that curls electrons into microwaves, guitar pickups, transformers that trade volts for turns, and hard disks that store a trillion tiny magnets per square inch.

explainer.title: Earth, hot iron and two myths
explainer.text: The Earth's field is tilted, wanders and has flipped many times; it shields us and lights the aurora. Iron is magnetic because its domains line up, until 770 °C. Break a magnet and you get two magnets, and magnet bracelets have no proven healing power.

concepts.def: The region round a magnet or current where magnetic forces act, with a strength and a direction.
The SI unit of magnetic field (flux density). Earth ≈ 50 µT; an MRI 1.5–3 T.
The north and south ends of a magnet. Like poles repel, unlike poles attract, and they always come in pairs.
A coil, usually round an iron core, that is a magnet only while current flows: B = μ₀ n I inside.
A current in a field feels a force F = B I L at right angles to both, shown by Fleming's left-hand rule.
Tiny regions in iron where the atoms' magnets all point one way. Lining them up magnetises the iron.
The temperature above which a ferromagnet loses its magnetism: 770 °C for iron.
The bubble of the Earth's field in space that turns aside the solar wind and guides the aurora.
